title: fix: cuda-graph capture/replay shape-guard warmup regression and scheduling fallback
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: A customer-facing regression was observed when using CUDA graph capture/replay with shape guards + warmup. Under certain token-length distributions the capture graph would be recorded with an incorrect shape-guard path leading to silent KV cache corruption or OOMs on replay. This PR fixes the root cause and adds safer fallbacks and more deterministic warmup behavior.

Summary of changes: 1) Make shape-guard checks deterministic during capture by normalizing sequence-length batches and inserting a no-op "shape-guard-warmup" pass before final capture. 2) Add an explicit scheduling fallback: if replay detects a guard mismatch it will invalidate the captured graph and fall back to the non-graph path (with a single re-capture attempt), avoiding long-running corrupted replays. 3) Update kernel selection to prefer quantized-friendly kernels when shape guards indicate stable seqlen ranges. 4) Improve logging/metrics around capture/replay attempts and guard mismatches for easier SRE debugging.

Checklist: - [x] Add unit tests for guard mismatch detection and fallback - [x] Add integration test exercising capture->replay across varying seq lengths - [x] Manual reproduce+fix of OOM customer case - [x] CI green + perf regression check (no measurable latency regression for stable workloads)

Testing: Ran perf-canary batch (N=1200 requests) across sequence-length distribution mixes; verified no OOMs and identical top-k token outputs post-replay within numerical tolerance. Verified CI E2E and GPU unit tests.

Impact: Fixes intermittent OOMs and mis-routed KV cache states when using CUDA graph capture in presence of shape guards. Slight increase in capture-time (~1-2ms per capture) due to the warmup pass but preserves end-to-end latency and throughput in steady-state.

- Fix: Prevent intermittent OOMs and KV-cache corruption when using CUDA graph capture/replay with shape guards by adding a deterministic warmup pass and safer replay fallback.
